value.a:
THE ONE REAL CANDIDATE, and the whys separate it. cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py's discipline paragraph says instrumentation is 'targeted and TEMPORARY... not standing probes left hanging: a permanent firehose turns CC's mailbox into noise', citing the shrinking-footprint principle. A standing emitter on the inference path is permanent by construction, so on its face this collides with the floor's own charter. IT IS NOT EXCLUSIVE-AND-TERMINAL, and the reason is in that same file's history rather than in my reading of it: the paragraph was written when home was CC's in-memory MAILBOX, and its concern is a live process being flooded. The file's own 'WHAT THAT REPLACED' section records that home became a FILE on 2026-08-18 and that the plug outlived the socket. A file that a 30-day sweep forgets — child (3) of this same parent — has no firehose to be. What survives from that paragraph is the GRAIN bound, not the duration bound: 'never every function call, or every heartbeat', which is Akien's own wording in the brief that bore the parent. THE DISTINCTION TO RECORD: the discipline paragraph's 'temporary' is about a TARGETED instrument placed to catch a specific flake, and this is a STANDING trail at a named boundary. Both are legitimate and they are different acts; the file does not yet say so, and that is a charter delta the build owes.

CHECKED AND CLEAR, TWO MORE. (i) import_sieve is the sole path to the inference host — this adds no route: a module-scoped trail reaches cairn.tools.base.address and cairn.tools.base.breadcrumb_log, both leaves at the floor, and opens no socket. (ii) diagnostic.py's boot-order law ('stdlib only, no DB, no loguru, no sink backend') — already re-measured and restated in that file on 2026-08-18 for exactly these two in-house imports; this cast adds nothing beyond them.

NO COLLISION WITH SIBLING CHILDREN: (1) a-device-logs-without-being-wired is DONE and is what this composes; (3) the-logs-tree-forgets-after-30-days sweeps the root this writes into and is uncast; (4) a-proof-cannot-seed-the-tree-it-reads is built and is why a proof of this one cannot seed the tree it reads.

THE ASSUMPTION THAT DIED DURING THE COMPLETENESS CHECK, recorded because it makes the claim smaller and truer. I had taken it that BreadcrumbLog was reachable only through DiagnosticBase, which would have made the floor work mandatory before anything could log. It is not — BreadcrumbLog(device, instance) is a plain constructor and any module can build one and hand it a record TODAY, with no new code. So the floor seam is not load-bearing for 'can a module log at all'; it is load-bearing for 'is there exactly ONE author of the record shape', since the shape (ts/us/source/gate/pointer/values/home) is built inside DiagnosticBase.emit and a second author is a second thing to keep in step with the inspector that reads it.

THE GRAIN DECISION, made at this cast rather than left to the build: ONE record per inference call at the outcome, carrying the host that answered and the rungs walked past as a VALUE on that record — never one record per rung. /intent left these in unnoticed tension (its falsifier wanted 'which host answered', its wrong-intent clause forbade a record per rung), and host.py's resolver WALKS rungs cheapest-first on HostUnreachable, so the two collide in the ordinary case. A walk is one crossing with a path, not three crossings. This keeps an ordinary cheapest-first resolution from reading as three failures while still answering 'why was it slow'.

AT THE CLOSE (2026-08-18): THE BUILD IS DEVICE-LOCAL, NOT A FLOOR SEAM, AND THE THREE RECORDS NOW SAY SO. The cast and constrain both opened on 'cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py — a module-scoped trail', on orient's premise that a component without a device class cannot reach its trail. THE SURVEY MEASURED THAT PREMISE FALSE (its fifth absence, driven rather than reasoned at n=1: a DiagnosticBase subclass carrying cairn.devices.inference_domain.domain as its __module__, set_diagnostic_roots(tmp), one emit → home='sent' and a file on disk that did not exist before the call). So the build filled LESS than the bounds allowed: a private subclass in domain.py and three emit sites, and NOTHING under cairn/tools/. Measured at acceptance: `git diff --stat 9163ffc..HEAD -- cairn/tools/` prints nothing. A shared floor helper is still genuinely absent in the narrow sense — the one prior user hand-rolls the same five lines — but the absence is DUPLICATION AT n=2, not inability, and build-minimal does not buy an abstraction for a second user. Read the `children` field above as the cast-time premise, corrected here, not as the shape of what was built.

SPEND CAME OFF THE TRAIL, AND THE MEASUREMENT KILLED IT RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. The first build put the stored cost and the avoided counter on the hit line; the line came back DEGRADED — BreadcrumbLog replaced `values` with {} plus `values_unwritable`, because a postgres Decimal is not JSON and the trail is a JSONL file. The available fix was to coerce; the right fix was to CUT. The row already holds the spend the line points at, and one number kept in two records is a number that can drift — which is precisely what this ticket's own agreement clause (c) forbids. THE SPLIT, now a regression tooth: THE TRAIL SAYS WHAT THE CALL DID; THE METER SAYS WHAT IT COST.

THIS BUILD REPRODUCED a-proof-cannot-seed-the-tree-it-reads AND THEN GAVE IT A NEW MOUTH. Running the six standing device proofs BARE during the build wrote 24 records into the LIVE ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/diagnostics.jsonl — 14 miss / 6 hit / 4 refused, every miss naming host='fake-host', all inside 0.3 seconds — spoiling this ticket's own before-witness (censused, then moved aside through bin/cmd/trash, and the witness re-taken). The new mouth is measured and permanent: under the tester's instance seal, test_inference_domain.py now reports wrote_to_instance count 1, path 'logs/inference_domain/0/diagnostics.jsonl' — a proof that never touched the logs tree before this voyage now writes to it, and the ONLY thing keeping that out of the live tree is the seal. THE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, and it is now a standing fact about this device: A PROOF OF inference_domain MUST BE RUN UNDER THE TESTER, NEVER BARE. Its probe reads the live trail against the live store, so a bare run does not merely litter — it feeds the instrument false population.

THE FLOOR'S DISCIPLINE PARAGRAPH IS OWED A DELTA THIS VOYAGE DELIBERATELY DID NOT WRITE. cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py says instrumentation is 'targeted and TEMPORARY... not standing probes left hanging'; this is a STANDING trail at a named boundary, and both acts are legitimate. Writing that distinction into diagnostic.py would have put a diff hunk under cairn/tools/ and falsified this ticket's own criterion 5 instrument at the moment it was measured. Recorded in inference_domain's charter (how_it_learns) where it costs nothing, and owed as a separate act at the floor's own address rather than smuggled in here.

THE TOOL CALLS AS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE CHART (/sail step 9, a hand's act — nothing counts or observes them yet; ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart). THE COUNT FIRST, because it needs no judgement: roughly 90 tool calls between the validate berth and done, hand-counted across a compaction boundary and therefore an estimate rather than a measurement — high for a build this small, and the score reads DOWNWARD on the packet. FIVE NAMED FALSIFICATIONS, each with the leg it indicts. (1) ORIENT: its premise that a component without a device class cannot reach its trail — falsified by the survey's own driven n=1 (a DiagnosticBase subclass carrying domain as __module__, one emit, home='sent', a file on disk). (2) CONSTRAIN: its `in` list opened with a floor seam authored from that false premise, so the bounds licensed a build twice the size of the one needed. (3) VALIDATE, criterion 5: `grep -n '\"inference_domain\"' domain.py` was authored without opening domain.py, where CACHE_OWNER already matched — an instrument that cannot pass on a file it never read. (4) HYPOTHESIZE, piece 7: its non-vacuity instrument specified removing the emit and re-running BY HAND, which is a hand act on the code under test rather than a tooth; what shipped moves the world instead and runs on every future invocation. (5) VALIDATE, criterion 6: it named 'the emit chokepoint at the WATCHME crossing' as the instrument, but the emission gate renders on the crossing OFF WatchMe — at PROVED, which is AFTER the verdict that must carry the measurement. The chart authored an obligation whose instrument could not run before the artifact that reports it; the fix was to call transitions.inspect_emission directly. AND ONE FINDING ABOUT THE SURVEY STAGE ITSELF, not about this voyage: every file opened at the close — verdict.py, transitions.py, clearance.py, validation_store.py — was absent from survey's holdings, because survey inventories what the BUILD composes and says nothing about what the CLOSE needs. So the close's doors get re-derived every voyage, which is Law 1's defect wearing a routine face.
